answer.read: Opening round. The supplier quotes €6.05 with no clause, 30 d payment and 12 months [S]. That sits far above the €5.45 we pay today and our last orders [D a5]. Its cost story leans on twelve-month rises [S], but the alloy index fell 5.5% since June [a1] and PPI-C2431 fell 2.3% [a4]. It also says its material is covered at fixed prices until March 2027 [Z], so short-term index moves barely touch it. Earlier it proposed agreeing a price basis with an AS-14404 clause [Z], which suggests it wants longer-term stability and index protection. Its OTD of 88% is below our target [a2]. Its own unsolicited quote at €5.45 [Z quote:7300008] shows €6.05 is padded.
answer.message: Thank you for your offer. We cannot recognise the requested increase: the alloy surcharge has been falling in recent months, your material is secured at fixed prices into next year, and our recent orders were placed well below your quotation. In addition, delivery performance has not met our expectations. We are prepared to offer a longer commitment and extended payment terms on the basis set out in the attached term sheet.
answer.reason: E0 and o9 tie for the lowest C (€952,980), well below any 12-month option at about €1.035M. The long term gives the supplier volume security, partly offsetting its cash cost under 90 d payment. A clause would add cost for us while its material is covered, so we leave it out. Citing the falling index, our €5.45 order history and the OTD shortfall anchors the price. E0's 36 months suits a goal of leverage at the same C as o9.
